title: Every Pure Nash Equilibrium of Round-Robin with Three Agents and Seven Goods Is Envy-Free up to One Good
abstract: Under the Round-Robin picking-sequence mechanism for allocating indivisible goods, agents take turns selecting items according to a fixed cyclic sequence. When agents report rankings strategically rather than sincerely, the mechanism induces a normal-form game. In arXiv:2610.23686, Proposition 1 shows that pure Nash equilibria need not be envy-free up to one good (EF1), presenting an eight-good counterexample with three agents under additive valuations. We prove that for three agents and seven goods, every pure Nash equilibrium of Round-Robin with nonnegative additive valuations is EF1. Together with the fact, also proved here, that every equilibrium is EF1 when the number of goods is at most twice the number of agents (up to six goods for three agents), this shows that the eight-good counterexample of arXiv:2610.23686 uses the fewest goods possible for three agents. Envy toward an agent who picks at most twice is ruled out by a single deviation: the envious agent ranks first a good of that bundle still available at its first turn. Envy toward the agent who picks three times is ruled out by comparing the equilibrium with at most three explicit two-good deviations. The result has been formalized and mechanically checked in Lean 4.
introduction:
Fair division of indivisible goods studies the problem of distributing a finite collection of items among a finite set of agents in a manner that satisfies formal criteria of fairness. A central fairness notion in this domain is envy-freeness up to one good (EF1). An allocation is said to be EF1 if any envy an agent $i$ might have toward another agent $j$ can be eliminated by removing a single item from $j$'s assigned bundle. When agents have additive valuations, an EF1 allocation is guaranteed to exist.

A standard protocol for finding fair allocations of indivisible goods is the Round-Robin mechanism, a specific instance of a picking-sequence mechanism. In Round-Robin, agents are ordered cyclically—for example, $0, 1, \dots, n-1, 0, 1, \dots$—and at each turn, the designated agent chooses their favorite item among those remaining. When agents act sincerely by selecting their most preferred available good according to their true valuations, the resulting allocation is guaranteed to be EF1 for all additive valuations.

In multi-agent settings, however, agents may behave strategically rather than sincerely. A picking-sequence mechanism induces a normal-form game in which each agent submits a full ranking of the goods as their strategy. The mechanism then executes the sequence deterministically: at each turn, the active agent takes the highest-ranked good in their submitted list that has not yet been selected by any prior agent. An agent who understands the preferences and actions of others may be able to manipulate their reported ranking to secure a strictly more valuable bundle. A profile of reported rankings is a pure Nash equilibrium if no agent can unilaterally alter their reported ranking to obtain a bundle of strictly greater true value. This leads to the question of whether the fairness guarantees of sincere play persist in strategic equilibrium: is every allocation obtained at a pure Nash equilibrium of the Round-Robin mechanism EF1?

This question was examined in arXiv:2610.23686 ("Revisiting the Fairness of Pure Nash Equilibria of Round-Robin"). In Proposition 1 of arXiv:2610.23686, the authors construct an instance with $n = 3$ agents and $m = 8$ indivisible goods possessing a pure Nash equilibrium whose outcome allocation fails to be EF1. The paper describes this counterexample as establishing the failure of exact EF1 "with very few goods," but does not say whether fewer goods would suffice.

A first positive answer, for general $n$, is easy to obtain and is also formalized here: whenever the number of goods $m$ satisfies $m \le 2n$, every pure Nash equilibrium of Round-Robin under nonnegative additive valuations is guaranteed to be EF1. This result, formalized as `round_robin_pne_ef1_of_card_le_two_mul`, covers cases where every agent is allocated at most two goods. For $n = 3$ agents, the condition $m \le 2n$ ensures that every pure Nash equilibrium is EF1 for all instances with $m \le 6$ goods.

This leaves the case of $n = 3$ agents and $m = 7$ goods, the smallest case of the question whether Round-Robin pure Nash equilibria are always EF1 when the number of goods is at most $2n + 1$. Because $m = 8$ yields a counterexample for $n = 3$, the case $m = 7$ is the only one between the two.

In this post, we present the formalized theorem `round_robin_three_agents_seven_goods_pne_ef1`, which proves that for three agents and seven goods, every pure Nash equilibrium of Round-Robin with nonnegative additive valuations produces an EF1 allocation. A direct corollary of this theorem is that the eight-good counterexample in Proposition 1 of arXiv:2610.23686 uses the smallest possible number of goods for three agents: no counterexample with three agents can exist for seven or fewer goods.
result:
The main theorem formalizes that every pure Nash equilibrium of the Round-Robin mechanism with three agents and seven goods is envy-free up to one good.

Theorem (`round_robin_three_agents_seven_goods_pne_ef1`). Let $w : \text{Fin } 3 \to \text{Fin } 7 \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfy $0 \le w(i, g)$ for all $i \in \text{Fin } 3$ and $g \in \text{Fin } 7$. Let $\text{rank} : \text{Fin } 3 \to (\text{Fin } 7 \simeq \text{Fin } 7)$ be a reported ranking profile that is a pure Nash equilibrium for the Round-Robin sequence:
$$\text{is\_picking\_sequence\_pne } (w.\text{toValuation}) \ (\text{round\_robin\_sequence } 3\ 7) \ \text{rank}.$$
Then the resulting allocation satisfies envy-freeness up to one good:
$$\text{SocialChoice.FairDivision.Indivisible.IsEF1 } (w.\text{toValuation}) \ (\text{picking\_sequence\_outcome } (\text{round\_robin\_sequence } 3\ 7) \ \text{rank}).$$

The Lean statement formalizes agents as $\text{Fin } 3$ and goods as $\text{Fin } 7$, quantifies universally over nonnegative weight functions $w$ and report profiles $\text{rank}$, assumes the equilibrium hypothesis `is_picking_sequence_pne` on the sequence `round_robin_sequence` for 3 agents and 7 goods, and concludes that `SocialChoice.FairDivision.Indivisible.IsEF1` holds for the outcome allocation returned by `picking_sequence_outcome`.

Combined with what was known, this gives the following picture for three agents:

- The general theorem `round_robin_pne_ef1_of_card_le_two_mul` establishes that whenever $m \le 2n$, every pure Nash equilibrium of Round-Robin is EF1 under nonnegative additive valuations. For three agents ($n = 3$), this general bound covers all instances with $m \le 6$ goods.

- Proposition 1 of arXiv:2610.23686 provides an instance with $n = 3$ agents and $m = 8$ goods where a pure Nash equilibrium yields an allocation that violates EF1.

- Theorem `round_robin_three_agents_seven_goods_pne_ef1` bridges the gap between $m \le 6$ and $m = 8$ by proving that EF1 holds at every pure Nash equilibrium when $m = 7$.

Taken together: every pure Nash equilibrium of Round-Robin with three agents is EF1 for all $m \le 7$, while a non-EF1 equilibrium exists for $m = 8$. Hence eight is the least number of goods for which a Round-Robin equilibrium with three agents can fail EF1, and the counterexample of arXiv:2610.23686 is as small as possible. (Whether non-EF1 equilibria exist for three agents and every $m \ge 9$ is not addressed here.)
proof:
Proof Idea.
Write $A$ for the allocation returned by `picking_sequence_outcome` on `round_robin_sequence` for 3 agents and 7 goods. To establish EF1 we must show that for every pair of distinct agents $i, j \in \text{Fin } 3$ with $A_j$ nonempty, some $g \in A_j$ satisfies $v_i(A_j \setminus \{g\}) \le v_i(A_i)$.
The sequence is $[0, 1, 2, 0, 1, 2, 0]$: agent 0 picks at turns 0, 3, 6, agent 1 at turns 1, 4, and agent 2 at turns 2, 5. Write $x_1, y_2, z_3, x_4, y_5, z_6, x_7$ for the goods picked at the seven turns of the equilibrium run, so that
$$A_0 = \{x_1, x_4, x_7\}, \qquad A_1 = \{y_2, y_5\}, \qquad A_2 = \{z_3, z_6\}.$$
Four of the six directed pairs, those with $j \in \{1, 2\}$, are settled by a general lemma about agents who pick at most twice. The remaining pairs $(1, 0)$ and $(2, 0)$ are settled by explicit deviations of the envious agent.

Supporting Lemmas.
Lemma 1 (`round_robin_pne_ef1_pair_of_count_le_two`). Let $n \ge 1$ and $m \ge 0$, let $w : \text{Fin } n \to \text{Fin } m \to \mathbb{R}$ be nonnegative per-item weights, and let $\text{rank}$ be a pure Nash equilibrium of Round-Robin with $n$ agents and $m$ goods. If an agent $j$ appears at most twice in the picking sequence,
$$(\text{round\_robin\_sequence } n\ m).\text{count } j \le 2,$$
then for every agent $i \neq j$ with $A_j$ nonempty there exists $g \in A_j$ such that $v_i(A_j \setminus \{g\}) \le v_i(A_i)$.
*Proof outline.* Agent $j$ receives at most two goods. If $|A_j| = 1$, removing that good leaves the empty set, of value $0 \le v_i(A_i)$. If $|A_j| = 2$: before agent $i$'s first turn (turn $i$), agent $j$ has picked at most once, since each agent appears once among turns $0, \dots, n-1$. So some good $b \in A_j$ is still unallocated when agent $i$ first picks. If agent $i$ deviates to a ranking with $b$ first, the turns before turn $i$ are unchanged and agent $i$ takes $b$; by nonnegativity the deviation bundle is worth at least $w(i, b)$. The equilibrium condition gives $w(i, b) \le v_i(A_i)$, and removing the other good $a$ of $A_j$ leaves $A_j \setminus \{a\} = \{b\}$.

Lemma 2 (`round_robin_pne_ef1_of_card_le_two_mul`). Let $n \ge 1$ and $m \le 2n$, let $w$ be nonnegative weights, and let $\text{rank}$ be a pure Nash equilibrium of Round-Robin. Then the resulting allocation is EF1.
*Proof outline.* With $m \le 2n$ every agent appears at most twice in the sequence, and the argument of Lemma 1 applies to every pair $i \neq j$.

Envy Toward Agent 0.
In both cases the good removed from $A_0$ is $x_1$, agent 0's first pick, and the claim is $v_i(\{x_4, x_7\}) \le v_i(A_i)$. Every deviation used is a ranking whose first two entries are two prescribed distinct goods; the other agents' reports stay fixed, so the run coincides with the equilibrium run until the deviating agent's choice first differs.

Agent 1 (the goal is $w(1, x_4) + w(1, x_7) \le w(1, y_2) + w(1, y_5)$):
1. Deviation $(y_2, x_7, \dots)$. Turns 0 to 3 are as in equilibrium, and at turn 4 the good $x_7$ is still free, so agent 1 obtains $\{y_2, x_7\}$. Equilibrium gives $w(1, x_7) \le w(1, y_5)$.
2. If $w(1, x_4) \le w(1, y_2)$, the claim follows. Otherwise, consider the deviation $(x_4, x_7, \dots)$: agent 1 takes $x_4$ at turn 1, and agents 2 and 0 then take some goods $a$ and $b$ at turns 2 and 3. If $x_7 \notin \{a, b\}$, agent 1 obtains $\{x_4, x_7\}$ and equilibrium gives the claim directly.
3. Otherwise consider the deviation $(x_4, y_5, \dots)$; turns 0 to 3 are the same as in step 2. If $y_5 \notin \{a, b\}$, agent 1 obtains $\{x_4, y_5\}$, and equilibrium gives $w(1, x_4) \le w(1, y_2)$, contrary to the case assumption.
4. So $\{a, b\} = \{x_7, y_5\}$, and agent 2's choice $a$ at turn 2 (with $x_1, x_4$ taken) is $x_7$ or $y_5$. But in the equilibrium run agent 2 chose $z_3$ at turn 2 while $x_7$ and $y_5$ were both available, so agent 2 ranks $z_3$ above both; and $z_3$ is still available at turn 2 of the deviation. This contradiction finishes the case.

Agent 2 (the goal is $w(2, x_4) + w(2, x_7) \le w(2, z_3) + w(2, z_6)$) is handled the same way, with the deviations $(z_3, x_7, \dots)$, $(x_4, x_7, \dots)$ and $(x_4, z_6, \dots)$; in the last step both $x_7$ and $z_6$ would have to be taken by agents 0 and 1 at turns 3 and 4, and agent 1's choice at turn 4 contradicts its equilibrium choice of $y_5$, which is still available.

Step-by-Step Proof of the Main Theorem.
The Lean proof of `round_robin_three_agents_seven_goods_pne_ef1` fixes agents $i, j$ with $i \neq j$ and $A_j$ nonempty, and splits on whether $j = 0$.
- Case $j = 0$: then $i \in \{1, 2\}$, and the two deviation arguments above apply.
- Case $j \neq 0$: Lemma 1 applies with $n = 3$, $m = 7$, since agents 1 and 2 each appear exactly twice in $[0, 1, 2, 0, 1, 2, 0]$; this count is checked by evaluation in Lean.

This covers all cases and completes the proof.
discussion:
The result presented here resolves the status of pure Nash equilibria of Round-Robin for three agents and seven goods, establishing that every equilibrium outcome is EF1. This closes the gap between the positive result for at most six goods and the counterexample with eight goods.

In Proposition 1 of arXiv:2610.23686, the authors construct an instance with three agents and eight goods having a pure Nash equilibrium that fails to be EF1. In that paper, the counterexample was described as using "very few goods," without addressing whether an even smaller counterexample could be constructed. Together with `round_robin_pne_ef1_of_card_le_two_mul`, which settles $m \le 6$, theorem `round_robin_three_agents_seven_goods_pne_ef1` demonstrates that eight goods is the exact minimum number of goods needed for a counterexample when $n = 3$. No counterexample with three agents can exist with seven or fewer goods.

What the result does not cover. The theorem determines the least number of goods for a three-agent counterexample; it says nothing about three agents with nine or more goods, and it does not resolve the case of $m = 2n + 1$ goods for $n \ge 4$ agents. The natural general question is whether Round-Robin pure Nash equilibria are EF1 whenever $m \le 2n + 1$:

- For any number of agents $n$, when $m \le 2n$, `round_robin_pne_ef1_of_card_le_two_mul` guarantees that every pure Nash equilibrium is EF1, because no agent picks more than twice.

- When $m = 2n + 1$, the picking sequence allocates three items to agent 0 and exactly two items to each of the remaining $n - 1$ agents.

- For $n = 3$, this corresponds to $m = 7$, which our theorem confirms is always EF1.

- For $n \ge 4$, whether every pure Nash equilibrium remains EF1 when $m = 2n + 1$ is left as an open question.

Open questions and future directions. Two directions are natural:

- Settling the bound $m \le 2n + 1$. A central question is whether the equilibrium analysis used for three agents can be extended to arbitrary $n \ge 4$ when $m = 2n + 1$. In that setting, only agent 0 receives three items while all other agents receive two items, so any potential EF1 violation must involve envy directed at agent 0.

- The threshold for counterexamples as a function of $n$. The counterexample in arXiv:2610.23686 with $n = 3$ agents uses $m = 8 = 2n + 2$ goods. Determining whether counterexamples to EF1 at equilibrium exist at $m = 2n + 2$ for all $n \ge 3$, or whether larger numbers of goods are required as $n$ grows, remains an open line of investigation.
preliminaries:
We work in the setting of fair division with indivisible goods, as formalized in Lean 4. Throughout, let $N$ denote a finite type of agents and $G$ a finite type of goods, each equipped with decidable equality.

Definition 1 (`SocialChoice.FairDivision.Indivisible.Valuation`, `SocialChoice.FairDivision.Indivisible.AdditiveValuation`, `SocialChoice.FairDivision.Indivisible.AdditiveValuation.toValuation`). An abstract valuation on agents $N$ and goods $G$ is represented by the structure `SocialChoice.FairDivision.Indivisible.Valuation`, which consists of a function $\text{val} : N \to \text{Finset } G \to \mathbb{R}$ assigning a real value to each pair of an agent and a bundle of goods. An additive valuation is represented by the structure `SocialChoice.FairDivision.Indivisible.AdditiveValuation`, which stores a per-item weight function $\text{weight} : N \to G \to \mathbb{R}$. The structure is lifted to an abstract valuation via `SocialChoice.FairDivision.Indivisible.AdditiveValuation.toValuation`, which defines the value of a bundle $S \subseteq G$ to agent $i \in N$ as the sum of individual item weights:
$$v_i(S) = \sum_{g \in S} \text{weight}(i, g).$$
We restrict attention to nonnegative additive valuations, meaning that $\text{weight}(i, g) \ge 0$ for all $i \in N$ and $g \in G$.
*Remark.* The valuation structures reside in the namespace `SocialChoice.FairDivision.Indivisible` to distinguish them from Mathlib's ring-theoretic valuations. The nonnegativity condition is imposed as a weak inequality $0 \le \text{weight}(i, g)$.

Definition 2 (`SocialChoice.FairDivision.Indivisible.IsEF1`). Let $v$ be a valuation and let $A : N \to \text{Finset } G$ be an allocation. The predicate `SocialChoice.FairDivision.Indivisible.IsEF1` $v\ A$ states that for all agents $i, j \in N$ such that $i \neq j$, if the bundle $A_j$ is nonempty, then there exists an item $g \in A_j$ such that
$$v_i(A_j \setminus \{g\}) \le v_i(A_i).$$
*Remark.* The definition includes an explicit guard that $A_j$ is nonempty. This condition is necessary because the existential quantification $\exists g \in A_j$ cannot be satisfied when $A_j = \emptyset$. Under nonnegative valuations, an agent assigns value at least 0 to their own bundle and value 0 to the empty set, so an agent cannot envy an empty bundle; the nonemptiness guard ensures that an empty bundle does not generate a spurious violation of EF1.

Definition 3 (`picking_turn`, `picking_sequence_outcome`). A picking-sequence mechanism allocates goods according to a predetermined sequence of agents $\text{seq} \in \text{List } N$. Each agent $i$ reports a strict ranking over all goods, represented as an equivalence $\text{rank } i : \text{Fin } m \simeq G$, where $\text{rank } i\ 0$ is agent $i$'s top choice. The allocation proceeds turn by turn via the transition function `picking_turn`. The state of the mechanism is a pair $(A, U)$, where $A : N \to \text{Finset } G$ is the current partial allocation and $U \subseteq G$ is the set of items already allocated. Given a reported ranking list $l$ for the active agent $i$, `picking_turn` finds the first good $g$ in $l$ that is not in $U$. If such a good exists, the state is updated to $(A[i \mapsto A_i \cup \{g\}], U \cup \{g\})$; if all goods in $l$ have already been allocated, the state remains unchanged.
The function `picking_sequence_outcome` folds `picking_turn` along the sequence $\text{seq}$, beginning with the initial state $(\lambda i.\ \emptyset, \emptyset)$, and projects the result onto the first coordinate to return the final allocation.
*Remark.* In this execution, the sequence $\text{seq}$ and the reported rankings are fixed, while the allocation state and the set of consumed goods vary with each turn.

Definition 4 (`round_robin_sequence`). For $n, m \in \mathbb{N}$ with $n > 0$, the Round-Robin picking sequence of length $m$ among agents $\text{Fin } n$ is defined by `round_robin_sequence` as the list of length $m$ whose $t$-th element, for $t \in \{0, \dots, m-1\}$, is $t \pmod n \in \text{Fin } n$.
For $n = 3$ and $m = 7$, the sequence is
$$[0, 1, 2, 0, 1, 2, 0].$$
In this sequence, agent 0 picks at turns $t \in \{0, 3, 6\}$ (3 turns), agent 1 picks at turns $t \in \{1, 4\}$ (2 turns), and agent 2 picks at turns $t \in \{2, 5\}$ (2 turns).
*Remark.* Agents are indexed from 0 to $n-1$, and turns are indexed from 0 to $m-1$.

Definition 5 (`is_picking_sequence_pne`). Let $v$ be a valuation, $\text{seq} \in \text{List } N$ a picking sequence, and $\text{rank} : N \to (\text{Fin } m \simeq G)$ a profile of reported rankings. The profile is a pure Nash equilibrium, written `is_picking_sequence_pne` $v\ \text{seq}\ \text{rank}$, if for every agent $i \in N$ and every alternative ranking $r : \text{Fin } m \simeq G$,
$$v_i(\text{picking\_sequence\_outcome } \text{seq} \ (\text{Function.update rank } i\ r) \ i) \le v_i(\text{picking\_sequence\_outcome } \text{seq} \ \text{rank} \ i).$$
*Remark.* The equilibrium concept uses a weak inequality: no agent can obtain a bundle of strictly greater value by unilaterally deviating to a different reported strict ranking.

zh.title: 三个智能体与七件物品下轮换机制的每个纯纳什均衡都满足至多一个物品的无嫉妒（EF1）
zh.abstract: 在分配不可分物品的轮换挑选序列机制下，智能体根据固定的循环序列依次轮流选取物品。当智能体采取策略性报告排序而非如实报告时，该机制诱导出一个正规形式博弈。在 arXiv:2610.23686 中，命题 1 表明纯纳什均衡不必满足至多一个物品的无嫉妒（EF1），并给出了在可加估值下包含三个智能体和八件物品的反例。我们证明了对于三个智能体和七件物品，非负可加估值下轮换机制的每个纯纳什均衡都是 EF1 的。结合本文同样证明的事实——当物品数量至多为智能体数量的两倍时（对于三个智能体即至多六件物品），每个均衡都满足 EF1——这表明 arXiv:2610.23686 中的八物品反例在三个智能体的情形下使用了可能的最少物品数。对至多挑选两次的智能体的嫉妒可以通过单次偏离排除：产生嫉妒的智能体将该物品包中在其自身行动轮次仍可选的一件物品排在最前端。对挑选三次的智能体的嫉妒则通过将该均衡与至多三个显式的双物品偏离进行比较予以排除。该结果已在 Lean 4 中形式化并得到了机器检查。
zh.introduction:
不可分物品的公平分配研究如何在一组有限的智能体之间分配有限的物品集合，并满足形式化的公平性准则。该领域的一个核心公平性概念是至多一个物品的无嫉妒（EF1）。如果智能体 $i$ 对另一个智能体 $j$ 可能产生的任何嫉妒，都可以通过从分配给 $j$ 的物品包中移除单个物品来消除，则称该分配满足 EF1。当智能体具有可加估值时，保证存在满足 EF1 的分配。

寻找不可分物品公平分配的一个标准协议是轮换机制，它是挑选序列机制的一个具体实例。在轮换机制中，智能体按循环次序排列——例如 $0, 1, \dots, n-1, 0, 1, \dots$——并且在每个轮次中，指定的智能体在剩余物品中选择自己最偏好的物品。当智能体表现诚实，即根据其真实估值选择最偏好的可用物品时，所得到的分配对于所有可加估值都保证满足 EF1。

然而，在多智能体设定中，智能体可能会采取策略性行为而非如实报告。挑选序列机制诱导出一个正规形式博弈，其中每个智能体提交所有物品的完整排序作为其策略。随后，机制确定性地执行该序列：在每个轮次中，当前行动的智能体在其提交的列表中选取尚未被先前任何智能体选走的最优物品。了解其他智能体的偏好和行动的智能体，可能能够通过操纵其报告的排序来获取真实价值严格更高的物品包。如果没有任何智能体能够通过单方面改变其报告的排序来获得真实价值严格更高的物品包，则称报告排序的策略组合为一个纯纳什均衡。这引出了一个问题：诚实参与下的公平性保证在策略性均衡中是否依然存在？即轮换机制的纯纳什均衡所获得的每个分配都是 EF1 的吗？

该问题在 arXiv:2610.23686（《Revisiting the Fairness of Pure Nash Equilibria of Round-Robin》）中得到了探讨。在 arXiv:2610.23686 的命题 1 中，作者构造了一个包含 $n = 3$ 个智能体和 $m = 8$ 件不可分物品的实例，该实例具有一个结果分配不满足 EF1 的纯纳什均衡。该论文将这一反例描述为用“极少数物品”确立了精确 EF1 的失效，但并未说明更少的物品是否足够。

针对一般 $n$ 的一个正面结论很容易获得，并且也在本文中得到了形式化：只要物品数量 $m$ 满足 $m \le 2n$，非负可加估值下轮换机制的每个纯纳什均衡都保证是 EF1 的。这一结果被形式化为 `round_robin_pne_ef1_of_card_le_two_mul`，涵盖了每个智能体至多分得两件物品的情形。对于 $n = 3$ 个智能体，条件 $m \le 2n$ 确保了对于所有物品数 $m \le 6$ 的实例，每个纯纳什均衡都是 EF1 的。

这便留下了 $n = 3$ 个智能体和 $m = 7$ 件物品的情形，即物品数量至多为 $2n + 1$ 时轮换机制纯纳什均衡是否始终为 EF1 这一问题的最小情形。由于当 $n = 3$ 时 $m = 8$ 给出了反例，因此 $m = 7$ 是二者之间唯一的情形。

在本篇博文中，我们给出了形式化定理 `round_robin_three_agents_seven_goods_pne_ef1`，该定理证明了对于三个智能体和七件物品，非负可加估值下轮换机制的每个纯纳什均衡都会产生满足 EF1 的分配。该定理的一个直接推论是，arXiv:2610.23686 命题 1 中的八物品反例对于三个智能体使用了可能的最少物品数：对于三个智能体，不存在七件或更少物品的反例。
zh.preliminaries:
我们在不可分物品公平分配的设定下展开工作，并在 Lean 4 中进行形式化。在整篇文章中，令 $N$ 表示智能体的有限类型，$G$ 表示物品的有限类型，二者均配备可判定相等性。

定义 1（`SocialChoice.FairDivision.Indivisible.Valuation`、`SocialChoice.FairDivision.Indivisible.AdditiveValuation`、`SocialChoice.FairDivision.Indivisible.AdditiveValuation.toValuation`）。智能体 $N$ 与物品 $G$ 上的抽象估值由结构体 `SocialChoice.FairDivision.Indivisible.Valuation` 表示，它由一个函数 $\text{val} : N \to \text{Finset } G \to \mathbb{R}$ 组成，为每个智能体与物品包的二元组赋予一个实数值。可加估值由结构体 `SocialChoice.FairDivision.Indivisible.AdditiveValuation` 表示，它存储了一个逐项权重函数 $\text{weight} : N \to G \to \mathbb{R}$。该结构通过 `SocialChoice.FairDivision.Indivisible.AdditiveValuation.toValuation` 提升为抽象估值，后者将物品包 $S \subseteq G$ 对智能体 $i \in N$ 的价值定义为各单件物品权重之和：
$$v_i(S) = \sum_{g \in S} \text{weight}(i, g).$$
我们将注意力限制在非负可加估值上，这意味着对所有 $i \in N$ 和 $g \in G$ 均有 $\text{weight}(i, g) \ge 0$。
*注。* 估值结构位于命名空间 `SocialChoice.FairDivision.Indivisible` 下，以区别于 Mathlib 中环论意义下的估值。非负性条件通过弱不等式 $0 \le \text{weight}(i, g)$ 加以约束。

定义 2（`SocialChoice.FairDivision.Indivisible.IsEF1`）。设 $v$ 为估值，并设 $A : N \to \text{Finset } G$ 为分配。谓词 `SocialChoice.FairDivision.Indivisible.IsEF1` $v\ A$ 表明：对于所有满足 $i \neq j$ 的智能体 $i, j \in N$，如果物品包 $A_j$ 非空，则存在一件物品 $g \in A_j$ 使得
$$v_i(A_j \setminus \{g\}) \le v_i(A_i).$$
*注。* 该定义包含一个显式的守卫条件，即 $A_j$ 非空。这一条件是必要的，因为当 $A_j = \emptyset$ 时，存在量化 $\exists g \in A_j$ 无法得到满足。在非负估值下，智能体对其自身物品包赋予的价值至少为 0，而对空集赋予的价值为 0，因此智能体不会嫉妒空物品包；非空守卫条件确保了空物品包不会产生虚假的 EF1 违背。

定义 3（`picking_turn`、`picking_sequence_outcome`）。挑选序列机制根据预先确定的智能体序列 $\text{seq} \in \text{List } N$ 分配物品。每个智能体 $i$ 报告一个在所有物品上的严格排序，表示为等价关系 $\text{rank } i : \text{Fin } m \simeq G$，其中 $\text{rank } i\ 0$ 是智能体 $i$ 最优的选择。分配过程通过状态转移函数 `picking_turn` 逐轮进行。该机制的状态是一个二元组 $(A, U)$，其中 $A : N \to \text{Finset } G$ 为当前的部分分配，$U \subseteq G$ 为已分配物品的集合。给定当前行动智能体 $i$ 的报告排序列表 $l$，`picking_turn` 寻找 $l$ 中不在 $U$ 内且排在最前的物品 $g$。如果存在这样的物品，状态更新为 $(A[i \mapsto A_i \cup \{g\}], U \cup \{g\})$；若 $l$ 中的所有物品都已被分配，则状态保持不变。
函数 `picking_sequence_outcome` 沿着序列 $\text{seq}$ 对 `picking_turn` 进行折叠，从初始状态 $(\lambda i.\ \emptyset, \emptyset)$ 开始，并将结果投影到第一个分量以返回最终分配。
*注。* 在此执行过程中，序列 $\text{seq}$ 和报告的排序是固定的，而分配状态和已被消耗的物品集合随着每个轮次而变化。

定义 4（`round_robin_sequence`）。对于 $n, m \in \mathbb{N}$ 且 $n > 0$，智能体 $\text{Fin } n$ 之间长度为 $m$ 的轮换挑选序列由 `round_robin_sequence` 定义为长度为 $m$ 的列表，其第 $t$ 个元素（对于 $t \in \{0, \dots, m-1\}$）为 $t \pmod n \in \text{Fin } n$。
对于 $n = 3$ 和 $m = 7$，该序列为
$$[0, 1, 2, 0, 1, 2, 0].$$
在此序列中，智能体 0 在轮次 $t \in \{0, 3, 6\}$ 挑选（共 3 个轮次），智能体 1 在轮次 $t \in \{1, 4\}$ 挑选（共 2 个轮次），智能体 2 在轮次 $t \in \{2, 5\}$ 挑选（共 2 个轮次）。
*注。* 智能体的索引从 0 到 $n-1$，轮次的索引从 0 到 $m-1$。

定义 5（`is_picking_sequence_pne`）。设 $v$ 为估值，$\text{seq} \in \text{List } N$ 为挑选序列，$\text{rank} : N \to (\text{Fin } m \simeq G)$ 为报告排序的策略组合。如果对于每个智能体 $i \in N$ 以及每个替代排序 $r : \text{Fin } m \simeq G$，均有
$$v_i(\text{picking\_sequence\_outcome } \text{seq} \ (\text{Function.update rank } i\ r) \ i) \le v_i(\text{picking\_sequence\_outcome } \text{seq} \ \text{rank} \ i).$$
则称该策略组合为一个纯纳什均衡，记作 `is_picking_sequence_pne` $v\ \text{seq}\ \text{rank}$。
*注。* 该均衡概念使用弱不等式：没有任何智能体能够通过单方面偏离到另一个不同的报告严格排序来获得具有严格更大价值的物品包。
zh.result:
主定理形式化了三个智能体和七件物品下轮换机制的每个纯纳什均衡都满足至多一个物品的无嫉妒。

定理（`round_robin_three_agents_seven_goods_pne_ef1`）。设 $w : \text{Fin } 3 \to \text{Fin } 7 \to \mathbb{R}$ 对所有 $i \in \text{Fin } 3$ 和 $g \in \text{Fin } 7$ 满足 $0 \le w(i, g)$。设 $\text{rank} : \text{Fin } 3 \to (\text{Fin } 7 \simeq \text{Fin } 7)$ 为报告排序策略组合，它是轮换序列的纯纳什均衡：
$$\text{is\_picking\_sequence\_pne } (w.\text{toValuation}) \ (\text{round\_robin\_sequence } 3\ 7) \ \text{rank}.$$
则所产生的结果分配满足至多一个物品的无嫉妒：
$$\text{SocialChoice.FairDivision.Indivisible.IsEF1 } (w.\text{toValuation}) \ (\text{picking\_sequence\_outcome } (\text{round\_robin\_sequence } 3\ 7) \ \text{rank}).$$

该 Lean 陈述将智能体形式化为 $\text{Fin } 3$，将物品形式化为 $\text{Fin } 7$，对非负权重函数 $w$ 和报告策略组合 $\text{rank}$ 进行全称量化，在 3 个智能体和 7 件物品的序列 `round_robin_sequence` 上假设均衡前提 `is_picking_sequence_pne`，并得出结论：`SocialChoice.FairDivision.Indivisible.IsEF1` 对 `picking_sequence_outcome` 返回的结果分配成立。

结合已知结论，对于三个智能体的情形可以得出以下图景：

- 通用定理 `round_robin_pne_ef1_of_card_le_two_mul` 确立了每当 $m \le 2n$ 时，在非负可加估值下轮换机制的每个纯纳什均衡都是 EF1 的。对于三个智能体（$n = 3$），该通用界涵盖了所有物品数 $m \le 6$ 的实例。

- arXiv:2610.23686 的命题 1 给出了一个包含 $n = 3$ 个智能体和 $m = 8$ 件物品的实例，其中纯纳什均衡产生的分配违背了 EF1。

- 定理 `round_robin_three_agents_seven_goods_pne_ef1` 通过证明当 $m = 7$ 时 EF1 在每个纯纳什均衡下均成立，填补了 $m \le 6$ 与 $m = 8$ 之间的空白。

综合来看：对于三个智能体，轮换机制的每个纯纳什均衡对所有 $m \le 7$ 都是 EF1 的，而对于 $m = 8$ 存在非 EF1 均衡。因此，8 是三个智能体下轮换机制均衡可能违反 EF1 的最少物品数量，arXiv:2610.23686 的反例已达到了可能的最少物品数。（对于三个智能体以及每个 $m \ge 9$ 是否存在非 EF1 均衡，本文未作讨论。）
zh.proof:
证明思路。
记 $A$ 为 `picking_sequence_outcome` 在 3 个智能体和 7 件物品的 `round_robin_sequence` 上返回的分配。为了确立 EF1，我们必须证明对于每对满足 $A_j$ 非空的不同智能体 $i, j \in \text{Fin } 3$，存在某个 $g \in A_j$ 满足 $v_i(A_j \setminus \{g\}) \le v_i(A_i)$。
该序列为 $[0, 1, 2, 0, 1, 2, 0]$：智能体 0 在轮次 0, 3, 6 挑选，智能体 1 在轮次 1, 4 挑选，智能体 2 在轮次 2, 5 挑选。记 $x_1, y_2, z_3, x_4, y_5, z_6, x_7$ 为均衡运行中七个轮次所挑选的物品，从而
$$A_0 = \{x_1, x_4, x_7\}, \qquad A_1 = \{y_2, y_5\}, \qquad A_2 = \{z_3, z_6\}.$$
六个有向对中有四个（即 $j \in \{1, 2\}$ 的情形）由关于至多挑选两次的智能体的一般引理解决。剩余的两个对 $(1, 0)$ 和 $(2, 0)$ 则通过产生嫉妒的智能体的显式偏离来解决。

支撑引理。
引理 1（`round_robin_pne_ef1_pair_of_count_le_two`）。设 $n \ge 1$ 且 $m \ge 0$，设 $w : \text{Fin } n \to \text{Fin } m \to \mathbb{R}$ 为非负单件物品权重，并设 $\text{rank}$ 为包含 $n$ 个智能体和 $m$ 件物品的轮换机制纯纳什均衡。如果智能体 $j$ 在挑选序列中至多出现两次，
$$(\text{round\_robin\_sequence } n\ m).\text{count } j \le 2,$$
则对于满足 $A_j$ 非空的每个智能体 $i \neq j$，存在 $g \in A_j$ 使得 $v_i(A_j \setminus \{g\}) \le v_i(A_i)$。
*证明概要。* 智能体 $j$ 至多获得两件物品。若 $|A_j| = 1$，移除该物品后留下空集，其价值为 $0 \le v_i(A_i)$。若 $|A_j| = 2$：在智能体 $i$ 挑选的轮次（即轮次 $i$）之前，智能体 $j$ 至多已挑选过一次，因为在轮次 $0, \dots, n-1$ 中每个智能体仅出现一次。因此当轮到智能体 $i$ 挑选时，某件物品 $b \in A_j$ 仍未被分配。如果智能体 $i$ 偏离到一个将 $b$ 排在最前端的排序，则轮次 $i$ 之前的轮次保持不变，智能体 $i$ 拿走 $b$；由非负性可知，偏离后的物品包价值至少为 $w(i, b)$。均衡条件给出 $w(i, b) \le v_i(A_i)$，而移除 $A_j$ 中的另一件物品 $a$ 后留下 $A_j \setminus \{a\} = \{b\}$。

引理 2（`round_robin_pne_ef1_of_card_le_two_mul`）。设 $n \ge 1$ 且 $m \le 2n$，设 $w$ 为非负权重，并设 $\text{rank}$ 为轮换机制的纯纳什均衡。则所产生的结果分配满足 EF1。
*证明概要。* 当 $m \le 2n$ 时，每个智能体在序列中至多出现两次，引理 1 的论证适用于每对 $i \neq j$。

对智能体 0 的嫉妒。
在这两种情形中，从 $A_0$ 中移除的物品均为 $x_1$（即智能体 0 在轮次 0 选取的物品），断言为 $v_i(\{x_4, x_7\}) \le v_i(A_i)$。所使用的每次偏离都是前两个条目为两个指定的不同物品的排序；其他智能体的报告保持不变，因此运行过程与均衡运行过程重合，直至偏离智能体的选择发生不同。

智能体 1（目标是 $w(1, x_4) + w(1, x_7) \le w(1, y_2) + w(1, y_5)$）：
1. 偏离 $(y_2, x_7, \dots)$。轮次 0 到 3 与均衡中相同，在轮次 4 物品 $x_7$ 仍未被选，因此智能体 1 获得 $\{y_2, x_7\}$。均衡条件给出 $w(1, x_7) \le w(1, y_5)$。
2. 若 $w(1, x_4) \le w(1, y_2)$，则断言成立。否则，考虑偏离 $(x_4, x_7, \dots)$：智能体 1 在轮次 1 选取 $x_4$，随后智能体 2 和智能体 0 在轮次 2 和 3 分别选取某些物品 $a$ 和 $b$。若 $x_7 \notin \{a, b\}$，则智能体 1 获得 $\{x_4, x_7\}$，均衡条件直接给出断言。
3. 否则考虑偏离 $(x_4, y_5, \dots)$；轮次 0 到 3 与第 2 步相同。若 $y_5 \notin \{a, b\}$，则智能体 1 获得 $\{x_4, y_5\}$，均衡条件给出 $w(1, x_4) \le w(1, y_2)$，这与情形假设矛盾。
4. 因此 $\{a, b\} = \{x_7, y_5\}$，并且智能体 2 在轮次 2 的选择 $a$（在 $x_1, x_4$ 已被选走的情况下）为 $x_7$ 或 $y_5$。但在均衡运行中，智能体 2 在轮次 2 选择了 $z_3$，而当时 $x_7$ 和 $y_5$ 均可选，因此智能体 2 将 $z_3$ 排在这二者之前；而在偏离的轮次 2 中 $z_3$ 仍然可选。这一矛盾完成了该情形的证明。

智能体 2（目标是 $w(2, x_4) + w(2, x_7) \le w(2, z_3) + w(2, z_6)$）以相同方式处理，使用偏离 $(z_3, x_7, \dots)$、$(x_4, x_7, \dots)$ 和 $(x_4, z_6, \dots)$；在最后一步中，$x_7$ 和 $z_6$ 必须均在轮次 3 和 4 被智能体 0 和 1 选走，而智能体 1 在轮次 4 的选择与其在均衡中对 $y_5$（此时仍可选）的选择相矛盾。

主定理的分步证明。
`round_robin_three_agents_seven_goods_pne_ef1` 的 Lean 证明固定满足 $i \neq j$ 且 $A_j$ 非空的智能体 $i, j$，并根据 $j = 0$ 是否成立进行分类讨论。
- 情形 $j = 0$：此时 $i \in \{1, 2\}$，上述两次偏离论证适用。
- 情形 $j \neq 0$：引理 1 在 $n = 3$, $m = 7$ 时适用，因为智能体 1 和智能体 2 在 $[0, 1, 2, 0, 1, 2, 0]$ 中各自恰好出现两次；这一计数通过 Lean 中的计算求值进行验证。

这涵盖了所有情形，完成了证明。
zh.discussion:
本文呈现的结果解决了三个智能体和七件物品下轮换机制纯纳什均衡的性质问题，确立了每个均衡结果都是 EF1 的。这弥合了至多六件物品的正向结论与八件物品的反例之间的空白。

在 arXiv:2610.23686 的命题 1 中，作者构造了一个包含三个智能体和八件物品的实例，其纯纳什均衡不满足 EF1。在那篇论文中，该反例被描述为使用了“极少数物品”，但并未探讨是否可以构造更小规模的反例。结合解决了 $m \le 6$ 的 `round_robin_pne_ef1_of_card_le_two_mul`，定理 `round_robin_three_agents_seven_goods_pne_ef1` 证明了当 $n = 3$ 时，八件物品恰好是反例所需的最少物品数量。对于三个智能体，不存在包含七件或更少物品的反例。

该结果未涵盖的内容。该定理确定了三个智能体反例的最少物品数量；它并未探讨三个智能体具有九件或更多物品的情形，也没有解决 $n \ge 4$ 个智能体下 $m = 2n + 1$ 件物品的情形。自然的普遍问题是：每当 $m \le 2n + 1$ 时，轮换机制的纯纳什均衡是否都满足 EF1：

- 对于任意智能体数量 $n$，当 $m \le 2n$ 时，`round_robin_pne_ef1_of_card_le_two_mul` 保证了每个纯纳什均衡都是 EF1 的，因为没有任何智能体挑选超过两次。

- 当 $m = 2n + 1$ 时，挑选序列将三件物品分配给智能体 0，并将其余 $n - 1$ 个智能体每人恰好分配两件物品。

- 对于 $n = 3$，这对应于 $m = 7$，我们的定理证实了此时始终为 EF1。

- 对于 $n \ge 4$，当 $m = 2n + 1$ 时每个纯纳什均衡是否依然为 EF1 仍是一个开放问题。

开放问题与未来方向。有两个自然的方向：

- 解决界限 $m \le 2n + 1$。一个核心问题是，用于三个智能体的均衡分析是否可以推广到 $m = 2n + 1$ 时的任意 $n \ge 4$。在该设定下，只有智能体 0 获得三件物品，而所有其他智能体均获得两件物品，因此任何潜在的 EF1 违背都必然涉及对智能体 0 的嫉妒。

- 作为 $n$ 的函数的反例阈值。arXiv:2610.23686 中包含 $n = 3$ 个智能体的反例使用了 $m = 8 = 2n + 2$ 件物品。确定对于所有 $n \ge 3$，在 $m = 2n + 2$ 处是否均存在均衡下违背 EF1 的反例，抑或随着 $n$ 的增长需要更多数量的物品，仍是一个有待探索的研究方向。
